scoring_key.resistance: LOW = additive, touches no gate/schema/claim/published artifact, rollback = revert one commit; MEDIUM = changes artifact semantics or an existing command contract; HIGH = changes what the repo asserts or invalidates an evidence chain
scoring_key.necessity: HIGH = without it a mandated acceptance read cannot pass; MEDIUM = removes a recurring false signal; LOW = hygiene only

items.root_cause: a generation-time identity is stored inside a commit-tracked artifact, so the committed value necessarily names the parent commit and no later regeneration can reproduce it (claims C-01..C-03)
items.precedent: the same class was already adjudicated in this repo: docs/ROUND3_DISCLOSURE.md item A6 (a tracked scan artifact recorded the scanned revision while being committed by a later commit) was fixed by renaming the field to source_revision_scanned and adding an explicit candidate_binding note, NOT by rewriting the generator; and tools/build_dist.py:192 already annotates its equivalent field as a legacy identity that is not the release tip (claims C-04, C-16)

options.change: (i) add an explicit --for-commit <sha> input to tools/admit_technologies.py (default = current behaviour) plus a documented canonical regeneration command; (ii) add a note naming the field's semantics, following tools/build_dist.py:192 and the docs/ROUND3_DISCLOSURE.md A6 rename precedent; (iii) machine check: the recorded candidate_head must be an ANCESTOR of HEAD; against the real data the value is 8ad0fd32..., 69 commits behind HEAD, so the originally drafted HEAD-or-HEAD^ rule was WRONG; (iv) machine check: the evidence manifest's per-entry sha256 must still equal the bytes on disk
options.effect: the volatile environment input becomes explicit and reproducible; a silent-staleness class becomes a red-light class; the verifier's literal read-only rule becomes satisfiable with no rule change
